objective_for_doctor:
Age: 43
Sex: F
Chief Complaint: pain improves when leaning forward

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have a sharp, knife-stroke type pain rated 7/10 that improves when I lean forward. It’s located in my right and left tonsils, the back of my neck, the palate, and the pharynx.

Do you have a fever, cough, runny nose, or trouble swallowing?
Do you have a fever, cough, runny nose, or trouble swallowing?
I don’t know. I do have difficulty swallowing, or a feeling of discomfort/blockage when swallowing.
Is the pain worse on one side than the other, and have you noticed any muffled voice, drooling, or trouble opening your mouth?

Yes—my pain is on both sides (right and left tonsils). I don’t know about muffled voice, drooling, or trouble opening my mouth. I have noticed my voice has become deeper, softer, or hoarse, and I produce more saliva than usual.
Have you had any shortness of breath, noisy breathing/stridor, or a feeling that your throat is closing?
I don’t know. I do have difficulty swallowing, or a feeling of discomfort/blockage when swallowing.
When did this start, and did it come on suddenly or gradually?
I don’t know. The pace at which the pain appear is 9 out of 10.
Have you had any recent fever or chills, and are you able to swallow liquids at all?
I don’t know. I do have difficulty swallowing, or a feeling of discomfort/blockage when swallowing.
Any recent sore throat or upper respiratory infection, dental infection, trauma to the throat/neck, vomiting, or eating something sharp like a fish bone?
Do you have neck stiffness or pain when moving your neck, and is the pain mainly in the throat or does it also radiate to the ears or chest?
Yes, I have pain in the back of my neck, and it improves when I lean forward. I don’t have it radiate to any of those places—it radiates nowhere.

[ABSTAIN] Too little discriminating information and several airway-threatening causes remain possible.
[POSSIBLE] epiglottitis/supraglottitis, retropharyngeal abscess, severe pharyngitis/tonsillitis, peritonsillar abscess, deep neck space infection
